title: The Build-Operate Divide: Bridging Product Vision and AI Operational Reality
talk_summary: A product lead at Free Play and a speech-analytics lead at Chime argue that GenAI products fail between V1 and V2 due to operational quality gaps, and that the fix is a tight iteration loop of monitoring, experimentation, and testing/evaluation with humans in the loop. They position existing QA/CX ops staff as the natural 'AI quality leads' who define what good looks like, build golden sets, and feed corrections back into the system.

takeaways.technique: Human-in-the-loop as feedback engine, not just gate
takeaways.what_they_do: Every human flag or correction of a model output is treated as a training/refinement signal that feeds back into prompts, evals, and model behavior, rather than a one-off approval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: think of human in loop not as like a safeguard it but as a feedback mechanism or feedback engine

takeaways.technique: Golden sets from real-world edge cases built by ops/QA
takeaways.what_they_do: Bring QA/ops people in early to define 'what good looks like' and build golden sets and tests against real-world edge cases, rather than only auditing after launch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: bring your like your ops teams and CX teams into the life cycle early to help what you know define what good looks like

takeaways.technique: Dedicated AI quality lead role (1-2 people)
takeaways.what_they_do: Formalize a role that owns labeling data, writing evaluation criteria, running experiments, and prompt engineering — explicitly not writing production code — and note 1-2 such people go a long way at small scale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: companies will have one person or two people in this role ... that goes a long way

takeaways.what_they_do: If resources are limited, insert human review only at high-risk, high-trust decision points, and make it substantive rather than for show.
takeaways.evidence_quote: looking at high-risisk, high trust areas is abs like an absolute must ... insert human in the loop at decision points and not just for show

takeaways.technique: Iteration loop as the ops function (monitor→experiment→test/eval)
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat product quality as a direct function of how fast the team can cycle monitoring, experimentation, and testing/evaluation, and staff that loop as an ops function.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your product quality becomes a direct function of your ability to move through this loop

takeaways.what_they_do: Argue that with the right tooling, people who don't write production code can still contribute hands-on via prompt engineering, labeling, and evaluation criteria.
takeaways.evidence_quote: writing production code is not the only way now that you can contribute in like a really hands-on way
